question: Does the collection-level 1917 transfer of Philadelphia Commercial Museum fishes to ANSP identify or plausibly locate Fowler’s historical Philippine eel specimen?

method.summary: Compared Sabaj’s published collection-code appendix, Fowler’s public unpublished Philippine-fishes manuscript and its BHL OCR, ANSP’s official collection-resource page, and bounded iDigBio API queries under the ANSP institution code. The review distinguishes the documented collection-level transfer route from specimen-level identity.
accessNotes: Sabaj (2020), Copeia 108(3), and Supplemental Appendix 1 were reviewed; the PCM entry is code 1920, p. 165.

The Smithsonian Institution Archives manuscript scan, digitized by BHL, and BHL item metadata/OCR were reviewed. Bounded searches for Monopterus, Fluta alba, Synbranchus, and eel returned no OCR matches; context shows other named eel entries carrying PCM references.

ANSP’s official Ichthyology information page was reviewed. Its departmental database link redirects to a public collections search portal, but the database itself was not independently queried with text tools.

The iDigBio public API query for Monopterus albus + institutioncode ANSP returned all 25 matches; none contained Philippines text in indexed record fields. Ophisternon bengalense + ANSP returned five rows, including Orion/Bataan 1923 (remarks: purchased) and four Malabon 1930 entries. The aggregator reports lastModified 2025-09-22.
No contact, email, scan request, payment, specimen loan, or access-control bypass was made. No raw response, archival scan, or image was retained.
method.reuseFinding: Only concise attributed collection-history and catalog facts are retained. BioOne limits article use to personal, educational, and non-commercial use; BHL reports no known restrictions as determined by the scanning institution. No independent rights determination or republication approval was made.

sourceFindings.scope: Sabaj’s appendix records the PCM’s extant fishes, mostly from the Philippines, as transferred to ANSP in 1917.
sourceFindings.limits: No specimen-level list, Fowler name, catalog number, or accession crosswalk is provided.
sourceFindings.attribution: A plausible historical collection route, not an individual specimen identification.

sourceFindings.scope: The later Fowler manuscript’s OCR places PCM references under Pisoodonophis macgregori and Pisodonophis boro; no direct Monopterus/Fluta alba hit was found in the bounded OCR name search.
sourceFindings.limits: Unpublished later manuscript and imperfect OCR; lack of a text hit is not proof of absence.
sourceFindings.attribution: Exclude these nearby passages as false matches to Fowler’s swamp eel.

sourceFindings.scope: ANSP maintains a public fish collection portal and says collection managers can supply up-to-date holdings information.
sourceFindings.limits: No specimen record or individual accession was found in the official overview page.
sourceFindings.attribution: A public search/holdings route only; no request was made.

sourceFindings.scope: The current aggregator query returns 25 ANSP Monopterus albus records with no Philippines text, and five Ophisternon bengalense records, one with Orion/Bataan 1923 and four with Malabon 1930.
sourceFindings.limits: Aggregator snapshot last modified in 2025; the query is not exhaustive and no result has a PCM/Fowler identifier.
sourceFindings.attribution: No specimen match found in this bounded search; do not claim the specimen is absent.

conclusion.decision: Sabaj documents a broad PCM-to-ANSP fish collection transfer, mostly involving Philippine fish holdings, but available sources and bounded public catalog searches do not identify Fowler’s swamp-eel specimen among those holdings. The 1917 route remains plausible at the collection level, while individual identity and custody stay unresolved.

scopeAndReuseDecision.decision: Research-only collection-history and public-catalog review. No species assertion, occurrence row, habitat, diet, fishery rule, safety statement, image, or public app projection.

nonClaims: No claim that Fowler’s specimen was transferred in 1917 or is currently held by ANSP.
No claim that the specimen is absent from ANSP; iDigBio and current-name queries are incomplete historical-collection screens.
The Ophisternon bengalense catalog results are not linked to the Fowler specimen or the reported 14 Smithsonian lots.
The Fowler manuscript PCM passages under other named eels are not a taxonomic or accession match for the swamp eel.
No date of introduction, collection waterbody, Pasig origin, native/introduced status, present-day presence, or public occurrence is asserted.
nextActions: If item-level identification remains necessary, locate a permitted Fowler 1918 page 62 scan or the PCM/ANSP accession ledger and search by the original Fluta alba name, the Fowler source note, specimen length, and any catalog identifier; keep the request unsent until explicitly authorized.
Treat the public ANSP departmental search as a route for future manual search. Its collection managers are listed for current holdings information; no email or request has been sent.
Continue the separate NCR freshwater/brackish/marine evidence work; this review does not change baseline or regional completion status.
